News.title: Miss England names TWO beauty queens joint winners in pageant’s first ever double-crowning
News.content:
TWO beauty queens have been made joint winners of a Miss England title for the first time in the pageant’s 98-year history.

Caitlin Bennett, 19, and Ellie Daglish, 23, finished in a tie after a catwalk and talent rounds.



Judges elected to have them share the Miss England East Midlands title and both qualify for the national final.

Reigning Miss England Grace Richardson, who hosted the event, said both “deserved to win”.



The duo will instead represent their counties, with Caitin as Miss Leicestershire and Ellie as Miss Nottinghamshire.

Student Caitlin, of Wigston, Leics, who is a part-time dance teacher, said: “I’m absolutely thrilled to have won my very first pageant at 19.



“Sharing the title with someone who has been with me since the very first audition makes it even more special and I’m honoured to be heading to the finals alongside Ellie, now a friend I’ve grown so close to.

“Graduating from my performing arts course the day before made this an unforgettable week and I can’t wait to see what the finals bring.”

Fashion merchandiser Ellie, from Nottingham, said: “The double crowning was something I never expected and I still can’t quite believe it.

“It’s been such a privilege to share this experience with Caitlin and I’m excited for what we’ll both achieve in our reign.”



The winner of November’s final in Leicester will represent England at Miss World 2027.

News.title: All MPs set to get round-the-clock security under Reform, says aspiring Home Sec Zia Yusuf as he unveils £100m plan
News.content:
ALL MPs would get round-the-clock security under a Reform government, says Zia Yusuf.

The party’s aspiring Home Secretary unveiled a £100million plan to beef up protection for politicians.



It follows Anne Widdecombe’s suspected murder.

Mr Yusuf denied Reform’s plans would mean pulling bobbies off the beat to protect politicians in Britain.



He also told The Sun: “I want to reiterate this is a place where we do need to spend money.

“I do not want to see another politician, regardless of party, or former politician, murdered.”

Mr Yusuf claimed attacks on Reform politicians as “racists” and “Nazis” were fuelling threats against them.

But he defended some of his spikier language after he previously accused Conservative politicians as “traitors” while calling some of his opponents “sick”.

Mr Yusuf said: “If you use the word traitor, for example, the definition of traitor is somebody who is engaged in betrayal.

“As far as I’m concerned it is demonstrable that the Conservative Party has acted in betrayal of the people who voted for them.”



It comes as a man has been arrested for allegedly threatening to shoot Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.

The suspect, in his 20s, is said to have made the death threat on X on May 8, the day after the local elections.

News.title: Convicted child killer Angharad Williamson plotting her freedom from behind bars after murdering son, 5
News.content:
A CONVICTED child killer is plotting her freedom from behind bars.

Angharad Williamson, 35, murdered son Logan Mwangi, five.



She was jailed for life in 2022 with a minimum 28 years.

She listened in from prison and was seen on screen at Logan’s pre-inquest review yesterday.



She was represented at Pontypridd coroner’s court by retired police officer Tony Thompson.

He told the inquest that he was looking into grounds for a review of the case.



He said: “We will see if there are grounds for an appeal to be put through the Civil Case Review Commission.”

He later said he had visited her in jail.

Logan was found in a river near his home in Sarn, Bridgend, in 2021.

Williamson was convicted with her partner John Cole, 44.



Schoolboy Craig Mulligan, who was 14 at the time, was also convicted.

A full inquest is due next year.

News.title: Cops have serious questions to answer over how their initial inquiry into Ann Widdecombe’s death was conducted
News.content:
Danger list

THERE can be no doubt that social media-fuelled extremism and violence is now a threat to our democracy.

The hundreds of death threats received by Reform UK leader Nigel Farage this year is appalling.



Just yesterday, a man was arrested for threatening to shoot him in the head.

Equally awful are the multiple rape warnings inflicted on female MPs from all parties every single day.



MPs on all sides are now at a greater risk than ever from warped keyboard warriors turned would-be attackers.

Spending on security may well need to go up to meet the growing challenge of keeping our elected representatives safe.



PM-in-waiting Andy Burnham has promised a proper review of a system that looks increasingly inadequate.

After the murders of three MPs in ten years, this clearly needs to happen.

Meanwhile, alarm is growing over how cops failed to recognise the possibility that Ann Widdecombe’s horrifying murder was a targeted attack.

So confident were they that this was a burglary gone wrong that Nigel Farage says Keir Starmer himself was briefed her killing was NOT politically motivated.



We now know counter-terror cops are looking into left-wing extremism as a possible motive and that other Reform figures may also have been targets.

As Farage pointed out: what ordinary burglar parks his car in the driveway and walks into the house?

Devon and Cornwall cops have serious questions to answer over how their initial inquiry was conducted.

Drilling down

DOES Andy Burnham really want to begin as PM by defying the will of the majority of voters?

A new poll reveals 58 per cent believe Britain should be drilling for its own reserves of oil and gas.



The public can see it makes total sense to be able to sell our own resources on international markets.

The cash could even be used to help get household energy bills down.

A failure by Burnham to persuade Ed Miliband to drop his opposition to North Sea drilling would be a massive early error.

Joy of Brex

REMOANERS who refuse to give up on their cherished dream of overturning Brexit might like to ponder the following.

Research out yesterday estimates the cost of Britain rejoining the EU today would be a staggering £37billion a year — or £711million per WEEK.



For context, that’s half the current defence budget or nearly two-thirds of all the money we spend in schools.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But for open-borders Leftists, any price is worth paying.

Even if it would leave Britain even more skint.

News.title: I hitched a ride from a secret serial killer who murdered seven strangers & planned to butcher me with a masonry hammer
News.content:
WATCHING a documentary about Ivan Milat – Australia’s worst serial killer – Colin Powis froze in horror.

Images of the fiend instantly took him back to 1982 when, as he backpacked in New South Wales, he had accepted a lift from a shifty stranger with a hammer stashed in his pick-up.





Colin, who was 21 at the time, had only arrived in Oz from County Durham two days earlier and recalled thinking the driver’s behaviour was “a bit odd”.

Fearing he was about to be robbed, he managed to flee the vehicle, but did not report his scare to police as he had escaped safely.

It was only when evil Milat’s face filled Colin’s TV screen eight years ago that he recognised him and realised he had escaped the clutches of a monster.

Milat murdered seven young hitchhikers, including two British women, in Australia between 1989 and 1993.

Cops now believe he could be responsible for as many as 50 murders, with definite links to 11.

A parliamentary inquiry Down Under has been considering if Milat could be behind more slayings.

Retired construction worker Colin, now 65, who lives near Durham, said of his close call with Milat: “It was a one-in-a-million chance he picked me up.

It was only when I saw a reconstruction of his murders on a documentary that my memory was triggered and I realised who it was.





“At the time, I thought he was some hillbilly who was going to rob me, but I now know I am lucky to be alive.”

Colin was one of millions of young Brits who travelled to Oz in the Eighties when backpacking became popular after the country brought in working holiday visas.

With no mobile phones and vast stretches of unoccupied land, tourists were an easy target for Milat.

He attacked young people travelling along the Hume Highway — the main route from Sydney to Melbourne — before dumping their bodies in the Belanglo forest.

His victims included Brit backpackers Joanne Walters, from Maesteg in Mid Glamorgan, and Caroline Clarke, of Farnham, Surrey, who met at a Sydney hotel in April 1992.

Milat picked up the two 22-year-olds and murdered them as they went fruit-picking in southern New South Wales.

Their bodies were found in makeshift shallow graves in a state forest reserve near Bowral, about 80 miles from Sydney, in September 1992, five months after they vanished.

Forensic evidence showed Joanne had been sexually assaulted, while Caroline’s body had decomposed so badly police were unable to tell if she had suffered the same ordeal.



Colin was travelling through the Blue Mountains to the mining town of Cobar in search of a job when roadworker Milat pulled over and offered him a lift.

He said: “It was about 10am and I was standing by the side of the road when he pulled over. In retrospect, he wasn’t at all normal, but I really needed the lift.

“I was going to throw my backpack in the back of the truck, which was open and virtually empty.

“The only thing I saw in it was a masonry hammer, which was lying in the corner. But Milat told me to put my bag in the cab behind the seats instead. Then he told me to put my seatbelt on. Back then, people didn’t put seatbelts on as a matter of course, so I thought it was a bit odd.

“A minute later, he told me to put the lock button down on the door. I thought, ‘Who does that? Nobody over ten years old’. I looked at him in a quizzical way and he said, ‘I don’t want you to fall out’.”

Chillingly, Milat then asked Colin how long he had been in Australia — and who knew he was in the country.

“After I said I didn’t know anyone, he went into a sort of trance state and more or less stopped talking to me,” Colin said.

And recalling how he tried to make small talk, he revealed Milat gave “short answers and grunted” during their 30-minute car trip.



“To be honest, I thought he was maybe drunk,” Colin admitted.

“I tried to humour him a bit, trying to make conversation. I asked him a bit about his background and he said his father came from Yugoslavia after the war. It later emerged this was true.

“We were going along the main highway and he suddenly said he was going to turn off on a dirt road because he wanted to check some animal traps he had set.

“He said I could come along if I wanted and ‘see some real Aussie wildlife’. Those were his exact words.

“I refused and said, ‘I want to carry on going’ and asked him to let me out. But instead of stopping, he continued slowly down the dirt road for about 400 yards before coming to a stop.

He said, ‘I’ll help you get your backpack’, and ran around the back of the pickup. He ran round to my side and by the time I’d got my backpack out he was standing there with his hands behind his back.

“It’s only now I realise he must have taken the hammer from the back and intended to bash me with it.”

Colin said the pair were disturbed when traffic diverted from the main road passed by.

He explained: “Luckily, the lights had changed and cars started driving slowly past us. If they hadn’t, I think I could have been killed.

“I remember I wasn’t that scared at the time. He was just a short fella and I was 21 and a good athlete, but I was worried he was going to steal my backpack and take my passport.



“As the traffic went slowly past us, I grabbed my bag and turned to walk away, but he tried to block my path. I shoved him with my shoulder and walked away.

“I was about 50ft away when he called, ‘Hey mate’. I looked back and he was lounging against the tailgate of his truck and shouted, ‘Have a safe trip’. He had a frustrated, wolfish look on his face.”

That was the last Colin saw of Milat and, despite hearing him named Australia’s most prolific killer, he thought little more about his encounter till the documentary aired.

The show featured another British male backpacker who escaped Milat’s murderous rage.

Paul Onions, of Birmingham, was offered a lift by the serial killer in 1990 and, spotting a rope and gun in the 4×4, he undid his seatbelt, jumped from the vehicle and ran.

Milat gave chase, firing his weapon, but Paul, who was 20 at the time, flagged down a passing motorist.

He went to Bowral police station and gave detailed information about Milat, including his job and the type of vehicle he drove.

But he was handed ten Australian dollars to get back to the British High Commission in Sydney and the report lay in a drawer for years.



Later, when Paul read newspaper stories about the remains of partially buried bodies in Belanglo State Forest, he called cops and reminded them of his ordeal.

Milat was arrested in 1994 and many of his victims’ possessions, including camping equipment and sleeping bags, were found at his home in Eagle Vale, New South Wales.

Weapons which fitted the killings were also discovered.

Finally, in 1996, Milat was convicted of murdering Joanne and Caroline — as well as Germans Simone Schmidl, Anja Habschied and Gabor Neugebauer, and Australians James Gibson and Deborah Everist.

An ongoing parliamentary inquiry into unsolved murders and long-term missing persons cases in Australia has heard how Milat, who died in jail in 2019 aged 74, could be behind more killings.

It heard from New South Wales homicide chief, detective superintendent Joseph Doueihi, who said a review into Milat involved assessing “50 or so” cases.

He said 11 files had been sent to the prosecutors’ office, which decided there wasn’t enough evidence to bring them to court.

Australian MP Jeremy Buckingham told The Sun: “It’s believed that Milat had strong links to organised crime.

“All seven backpackers he killed, except one, were last seen alive in the Kings Cross area of Sydney, which has been recognised as having some of the most corrupt policing in New South Wales.



“Milat was part of a paedophile ring and he was also involved in human trafficking.

“Joanne and Caroline may have spent time in captivity, where they were violated. There is forensic evidence that they dressed and undressed in multiple locations and one was murdered three months after the other one.

“Milat killed scores of people.

“An inquiry is under way. We are already receiving briefings from police and are planning to publish an interim report in August.

“There are also six public hearings scheduled all over New South Wales in coming months, where family members can present evidence.

“The final report probably won’t be completed for years.”

Meanwhile, in North East England, Colin is still coming to terms with the fact he could have been one of Milat’s victims.

He added: “I think he did kill more than he was convicted of. I just feel very, very lucky to have gotten away

News.title: Navy officer facing court-martial for ‘sexually assaulting junior rank 3 months after taking command of warship’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CAPTAIN'S TRIAL Navy officer facing court-martial for ‘sexually assaulting junior rank 3 months after taking command of warship’

A NAVY officer faces a court-martial for allegedly sexually assaulting a junior rank less than three months after taking command of a warship.

Lt Cdr Martyn Mayger became captain of HMS Tyne in February 2025.

But he was removed from post following a complaint and investigated by the Defence Serious Crime Command.



Lt Cdr Mayger never returned to command the vessel and has since been charged with two counts of sexual assault.



The preliminary stages of the trial will begin on July 17 at Catterick court martial centre, North Yorkshire.

HMS Tyne is one of three River-class offshore patrol vessels.

It regularly patrols the UK coast and the waters of northern Europe.

And has recently been monitoring Russia’s shadow fleet in the Channel.

The role includes protecting the UK’s critical infrastructure, such as undersea cables.

Last year, HMS Tyne shadowed Russia’s Kilo-class submarine Krasnodar in the Channel as part of a NATO mission.

The Ministry of Defence declined to comment further.



The Royal Navy has been rocked by a series of serious sexual complaints in recent years.

News.title: Britain faces eye-watering £35billion-a-year bill if it rejoins the EU, warn researchers
News.content:
BRITAIN faces a £35billion-a-year bill if it rejoins the EU, researchers have warned.

The eye-watering sum is nearly double the UK’s gross contributions before Brexit.



The estimate from pro-Brexit group Britain Unbound is based on Brussels’ proposed budget plans for 2028-2034.

Euro chiefs want to increase EU spending to almost €2trillion over seven years.



They also want to levy new taxes on carbon emissions, electronic waste, tobacco sales, and large corporations.

Britain Unbound boss Steve Wright said: “Those who wish to rejoin the EU should present their argument in the harsh reality of the present day.



“Not a rose-tinted picture of 2016.”

The figures are based on a hypothetical scenario where the UK joins the EU in 2028 ­without negotiating a rebate or opt-outs.

The findings are likely to fuel more scrutiny on Labour’s plans for Europe.

Incoming PM Andy Burnham once said he wanted the UK to rejoin the EU “in my lifetime”, but later rowed back.



Two weeks ago, Sir Keir Starmer’s EU negotiator Nick Thomas-Symonds called rejoining an “unrealistic mirage”.

Shadow Foreign Secretary Dame Priti Patel said it was clear a return to Brussels would mean “yet more tax rises”.

News.title: Disgust as grinning players hold 'Falklands belong to Argentina' banner after World Cup win against England
News.content:
Disgust as grinning players hold 'Falklands belong to Argentina' banner after World Cup win against England

Argentine players hold shocking banner on The Falklands after their World Cup win against England in a disgusting political act after the final whistle

View 6 Images Argentina's players hold a banner reading "The Malvinas (Falkland Islands) belong to Argentina," after win (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Argentina players were shockingly seen holding a flag saying The Falklands belonged to them as they grinned following a heartbreaking win against England.

‌



England were left devastated after the South American nation win 2-1 in the semi-final, in Atlanta, and took away the Three Lions' hopes of ending 60 years of World Cup hurt. The match quickly became heated with fights and clashes on the pitch between the two nations.

‌



Ahead of the match Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni said he was "not going to mix" politics and football but his players did not get the memo after waving a politically charged flag after the game.

‌



Heartbreak for England fans as World Cup final hopes slip through fingers after late Argentina goals READ MORE :

Harry Kane reveals Thomas Tuchel touchline message as England crumble late on vs Argentina READ MORE :

View 6 Images Players paraded around the pitch carrying the banner after their win against England (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Several Argentine players held a banner that read "Las Malvinas son Argentinas" which translated to "The Malvinas (Falkland Islands) belong to Argentina".

Argentina disputes British sovereignty over the islands and refers to them as Las Malvinas. Political tensions over the territory boiled over into conflict in 1982.

‌



View 6 Images Argentina players celebrate after their win (Image: AP Photo/Jacob Kupferman)

The Falkland Islands were uninhabited and unoccupied until they were first claimed by the British in 1765. In 2013 a referendum was held where islanders voted overwhelmingly to remain a UK overseas territory.

This stunt raises questions as FIFA's stadium code of conduct bans "banners, flags, flyers, apparel and other paraphernalia that are of a political, ⁠offensive, and/or discriminatory nature". Some Argentine players, following their quarter final win against Switzerland were heard saying: "For the Malvinas, for Diego [Maradona] and for Leo [Messi]'s last one."

‌



Some Argentina fans were also branded "disgusting" after booing England's national anthem before their semi-final. England's national anthem went first but was drowned out by the Argentine contingent in Atlanta, sparking a flurry of angry reaction from social media users.

View 6 Images Harry Kane and Dan Burn walk after the 2-1 loss as Argentine players celebrate (Image: AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

One user commented: "This (sic) Argentina fans are disgusting singing out loud and booing the England national anthem. Zero respect."

‌



Prior to the match, coach Scaloni said: "The reality is that this is a football match. I can't mix things up, especially out of respect for what happened so many years ago. It was a very sad period in our history, and there isn't much we can do about it, that's the reality."

View 6 Images Argentine fans in the stands hold up the 'Falklands are Argentinian' banner (Image: AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)

Despite these words from the head coach, Argentina vice-president Victoria Villarruel turned the build up political and said: "This is not just another match. I'm not going to be politically correct - against the English, it's always something more."

Article continues below

She added: "Long live Argentina! Because until our very last breath, we will reclaim what is ours."

View 6 Images Lionel Messi and Harry Kane after the match (Image: Getty Images)

The joyous mood after Anthony Gordon put the Three Lions ahead 10 minutes into the second half came crashing down as Enzo Fernandez equalised 85 minutes in. It soured even further when Lautaro Martinez put Argentina in the lead in the 92nd minute.

News.title: Heartbreak for England fans as World Cup final hopes slip through fingers after late Argentina goals
News.content:
England fans left with heads in hands scarcely believing eyes after devastating Argentina World Cup defeat

Devastated England fans have been left in tears after two dramatic late goals from Argentina saw the Three Lions' World Cup finals hopes come crashing down

View 9 Images England and Three Lions supporters have been left devastated after two late goals from Argentina (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

England crashed out of the World Cup in absolutely heartbreaking fashion. Two dramatic late goals from Argentina saw the Three Lions World Cup dreams end in a flood of tears. Despite going ahead in a dramatic semi-final, England came up short again. Both goals were scored in the last few minutes of the semi-final

‌



At the end the England players slumped to the pitch devastated by the defeat. They were so close yet so far to the World Cup final in New York on Sunday. Three Lions fans stood stunned with their heads in their hands scarcely believing what they had just witnessed.

‌



View 9 Images Anthony Gordon scored England's only goal against Argentina in a tense semi-final (Image: AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

‌



Harry Kane reveals Thomas Tuchel touchline message as England crumble late on vs Argentina READ MORE :

Despite being roared on by a 10,000 strong army of fans they were beaten 2-1 by Lionel Messi’s side. Mick Jagger, David Beckham and wife Victoria were in the crowd cheering England on. But were left devastated by the result.

England super fan Clive Heathcock, 69, from Crewe has been a Crewe Alexandra season ticket holder since 1977. He said: “To lose like that is just desperately sad. The lads did so well to get to the semi final. We may have fallen at the final hurdle but they’ve been brilliant all tournament. It’s just such a shame we couldn’t hold out until the end.”

View 9 Images Jordan Pickford consoled after game (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Lionel Messi sought out Harry Kane and gave him a huge hug.. There was an extraordinary and febrile atmosphere inside the magnificent air-conditioned stadium throughout.

England fans were far outnumbered by Argentinians. Some of the opposition fans wore shirts bearing the words “Hand of God” taunting Three Lions supporters about Diego Maradona’s controversial 1986 goal.

But England fans more than held their own by chanting throughout the match roaring Harry Kane’s men on. They sang the national anthem with particular passion and it was greeted with a huge roar at the end despite sustained booing from the huge Argentine support.

‌



View 9 Images Messi and Kane shake hands after game (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

There were England flags from every corner of the country fixed to the fences inside. I saw the towns of Blackpool, Wigan, Runcorn, Reading, Waterlooville and Corby represented. One fan stood forlornly outside the stadium with a sign saying: “Came here from Swindon still looking for a ticket that costs less than a car.” He didn’t get lucky.

Among the crowd were the O’Leary family from Harrow, north west London. Harry O’Leary, 16, was actually at his fifth major tournament. He was at the last World Cup semi-final in Moscow in 2018 when he was just eight-years-old with his mum and dad Ryan and Barbara.

‌



View 9 Images Thomas Tuchel, Manager of England, shakes hands with Nico O'Reilly #3 after the 1-2 loss during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Semi Final match between England and Argentina (Image: Getty Images)

He must be the youngest England fan in history to have attended two World Cup semi-finals. The family, Queens Park Rangers fans, only flew in the day before the game.

John Mills, 64, from Biddulph, near Stoke-on-Trent, Staffs is a consultant and is the safeguarding manager for British Ice skating. He is travelling with his great pal Brian Jackson, 75, from Mansfield, Notts, who is a retired project manager.

‌



View 9 Images England super fans John Mills and Brian Jackson

"It’s been such a great tournament and there’s been some great games. We came over for all the group games and then returned to England - we just couldn’t afford to stay for the whole tournament." Beforehand they made a visit to Martin Luther King’s birthplace before the match. He said: “We always try and do something different and historic when we go to the cities which host England games.

View 9 Images Argentina celebrate dramatic win (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



“Atlanta has always been associated with Martin Luther King. It’s been absolutely fascinating to see the house where he was born and the church where he preached. We’ve seen so many England fans here as well. Lots of us had the same idea.”

Graham Christopher, 68, from Macclesfield, said: “There have only been four World Cup semi finals played. 1966, 1990, 2018 and here today. It’s a real privilege to be here.”

The Three Lions supporters had patiently queued for an hour to get in then flooded onto the concourses three hours before kick off not wanting to miss a moment of the historic game. Back at home pubs were packed as 23 million fans watched the game in TV's highest audience for two years.

‌



View 9 Images Argentina's forward #10 Lionel Messi (L) and England's forward #09 Harry Kane (R) shake hands after the 2026 World Cup (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

One in three of the population tuned in to the BBC, with roads, railway stations and local supermarkets left deserted as the nation came to a halt. More than 14 million pints – six million more than normal – were drunk in boozers today. Another 16 million pints, seven million more than average, were downed at home.

Most were sold out and turning away customers. The Old Leyland Gates pub in Leyland, Lancs, wrote on Facebook: “We were fully booked, with an electric atmosphere roaring on England.”

Article continues below

View 9 Images Heartbreak for England (Image: Getty Images)

Before the game I saw Argentina fans waiting to have their photos taken outside a traditional red English phone box situated on Andrew Young International Drive. Opposite England fans were queuing for a beer at a bar called Tin Lizzy’s.

The Atlanta pubs have done a roaring business and will miss the travelling fans. There were pockets of trouble before game. But the worst was when the Argentina fans turned on each other. Followers of Huracan and San Lorenzo fought amongst themselves. Police arrested three and they will appear in court next week.

News.title: Donald Trump ‘leaning towards’ expanding Iran war ‘with ground troops’
News.content:
Donald Trump ‘leaning towards’ expanding Iran war ‘with ground troops’

Donald Trump is reportedly 'leaning towards' expanding the war on Iran, with the ceasefire in tatters and both sides launching missile attacks in recent days

View 3 Images Trump is reportedly 'leaning towards' expanding the war with Iran (file) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Donald Trump is reportedly "leaning towards" expanding the war on Iran after meeting with his top national security team - and could potentially deploy ground troops.

‌



Missiles have been launched by the United States and Iran over the past few days after the Trump said the fragile ceasefire with Iran was over last week as he lashed out at its leaders - calling them "scum".

‌



A naval blockade was imposed on Iran today and airstrikes have intensified in retaliation for Tehran’s attacks on ships trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. The American strikes hit an Iranian army barracks, killed at least seven troops and wounded more than 260 people across the country, Iranian officials said.

‌



View 3 Images A US Army CH-47 Chinook helicopter preparing to land in the Middle East during routine flight operations (file) (Image: US ARMY/AFP via Getty Images)

Ukraine hits over 100 Russian sea vessels in just days leaving Putin fuming READ MORE :

And now US officials have said Trump is "leaning towards" more extensive attacks rather than looking for peace after briefings from top aides, reports the Wall Street Journal.

Several options are reportedly on the table including greater airstrikes, sending ground forces to take islands by the Strait of Hormuz and bombing a fortified site that is suspected of being used for covert nuclear work.

‌



Trump is said to have held a meeting at the situation room in the White House where these possibilities were considered, including the potential bombing of the tunnel complex at Pickaxe Mountain - a nuclear-linked site the US is yet to target.

His vice president JD Vance was there, as were Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs Gen Dan Caine, CIA Director John Ratcliffe, White House envoy Steve Witkoff and other senior officials, it is alleged.

It is also reported that Trump hasn't made a final decision on next steps to take in the conflict.

‌



View 3 Images US aircraft carrier George H.W. Bush which is currently in the Middle East (file) (Image: US NAVY/AFP via Getty Images)

The US military said it launched two airstrikes against Iran on Wednesday, targeting Iran’s ability to stop shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. “We’ll find out whether or not we settle with them, or we just finish it off,” Trump said afterwards.

Iran’s paramilitary Revolutionary Guard threatened today to halt all energy exports from the Middle East over the blockade. “The export of oil and gas from the region will be either for everyone or for no one,” it said.

‌



While Trump also told Fox News that the US would hit Iran "hard" over the coming three days - and that there would be even wider strikes after that.

"Next week, it gets really bad for them because next week comes the power plants," Trump said. "Next week comes the bridges. We're gonna knock out all their power plants. We're gonna knock out all their bridges unless they get to the table and negotiate."

Already days of back-and-forth strikes by the US and Iran across the Middle East - and renewed threats to the waterway crucial to global energy supplies - have shredded the interim deal to end the conflict.

Article continues below

The US first imposed a blockade of Iranian ports in April and then lifted it last month after signing the interim deal that paused the fighting, and set a 60-day period for negotiations over issues such as Iran’s nuclear program. Those talks have stalled as fighting over the Strait of Hormuz has intensified.

News.title: Man, 31, banned from Royal Oldham Hospital after threatening to set it on fire
News.content:
Man, 31, banned from Royal Oldham Hospital after threatening to set it on fire

Andrew Stonier, 31, subjected staff at Royal Oldham Hospital in Greater Manchester to 'serious abuse and threats' before he was banned from the building until 2029

View 2 Images The man has been banned from Royal Oldham Hospital (Image: PA)

A man who threatened to set a hospital on fire and made repeated threats to staff has been banned from the premises for three years.

‌



Andrew Stonier, 31, subjected staff at Royal Oldham Hospital in Greater Manchester to "serious abuse and threats", Oldham Council said.

‌



The local authority sought a criminal behaviour order (CBO) against the man to protect NHS staff at the hospital until June 2029. This is a court order in England and Wales issued to tackle the most serious and persistent offenders involved in anti-social behaviour.

‌



Oldham Council said: "The order follows a series of incidents in which the offender made repeated threats towards nurses and hospital staff, including threats to set fire to the hospital.

View 2 Images Hospital staff were subjected to 'serious abuse and threats' (Image: STEVE ALLEN)

"This behaviour caused significant disruption as staff spent hours on end dealing with Stonier, diverting valuable time and resources.

‌



"As a result of the court order, the offender is prohibited from entering Royal Oldham Hospital until 28 June 2029, except in specific circumstances such as attending a pre-arranged appointment or requiring emergency medical treatment. A breach of the order will result in arrest."

As per the court order, Stonier must not enter Royal Oldham Hospital, including the clinical area, ward, department, A&E, and outpatient facility.

He can only attend the hospital for a pre-arranged appointment and must leave 30 minutes before and after. There is an exemption which only applies where "genuine emergency medical treatment is required".

‌



Anyone who breaches the conditions of a CBO faces further criminal action and could be returned to court, reports Manchester Evening News.

An Oldham Council spokesperson said: "This individual's behaviour towards dedicated NHS staff was completely unacceptable.

"No one should be subjected to threatening, abusive or intimidating behaviour while carrying out their job, particularly those working tirelessly to provide care to patients.

Article continues below

"These incidents placed an unnecessary burden on hospital staff and valuable NHS time and resources were spent dealing with his vile and threatening behaviour.

"We took robust action to secure this Criminal Behaviour Order, which sends a clear message that behaviour of this nature will not be tolerate and we will ensure that action is taken against anyone whose behaviour causes harm, fear or disruption in our communities."

News.title: Met Office forecasts exactly when third UK heatwave of 2026 will finally end
News.content:
Met Office forecasts exactly when third UK heatwave of 2026 will finally end

Met Office weather forecasters say a shift in high pressure could lead to temperatures cooling off across the UK by the end of this week - bringing a much needed reprieve for many

Met Office: Temperatures set to cool as weekend approaches

The Met Office expects temperatures in the UK to start cooling off by the end of this week as the third heatwave of 2026 comes to an end.

‌



Three scorching spells so far this year have brought record-breaking temperatures, leading to an increase in fires and ill health effects for many. But thankfully, forecasters expect a reprieve soon.

‌



In the Met Office’s latest Deep Dive weather forecast on YouTube, meteorologist Aidan McGivern explains that a shift in high pressure should mean that peak temperatures drop off on Saturday and Sunday.

‌



“High pressure, by the end of this week, is drifting towards the north-west, and that’s going to allow something a little fresher to recirculate around the high pressure,” he said. “Still above average temperatures for many, but by the time we get to Sunday those temperature anomalies are reducing.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

UK weather maps show new 36C heatwave surge with nine counties at 35C or more READ MORE :

UK weather maps show heatwave ending in 6C chill as 27 counties plunge below 10C READ MORE :

“So things are gradually cooling off for the rest of the week. It’s not going to be cold, neither is it going to be unsettled, but the high pressure is drifting into a position to allow something less hot to circulate around it.

‌



“We’re talking by Saturday and Sunday, temperatures in the mid to high-20s rather than the low-30s.” He explained the highest temperatures this weekend are expected in Wales and the south-west, with the lowest coming in the east and north.

The Met Office forecast issued this morning predicts highs of 29C in southern areas on Saturday, with 24C highs in northern regions. For Sunday, those peak temperatures drop to 25C in the south and 22C in the north.

View Image Temperatures should start cooling off by the weekend (stock) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



BBC weather forecast

BBC weather forecasters also expect temperatures to ease off towards the end of this week. They also say there’s a chance of some rain in places.

The BBC forecast states: “Friday looks to become less warm, with variable cloud in the north and sunshine elsewhere.

“Saturday is expected to bring more cloud, especially across northern and eastern areas. A few patches of light rain or drizzle are possible along the North Sea coast.

Article continues below

“Sunday looks to be mostly dry with variable cloud, and a chance of the odd shower in western England.”

News.title: Newlywed, 30, dies as bike ‘splits in two’ after crash with world champ skier
News.content:
Newlywed, 30, dies as bike ‘splits in two’ after crash with world champ skier

Laura Viktoria Hartig, 30, was cycling through the Dolomites in Italy during her honeymoon when she collided with a motorbike ridden by a former downhill skier

View 3 Images Laura Viktoria Hartig died shortly after her wedding (Image: Jam Press/@alltimelaura)

A newlywed fitness influencer has died after a horror road crash involving a former downhill skier.

‌



Laura Viktoria Hartig, 30, was critically injured in the collision with a motorbike while cycling through the Dolomites in northern Italy on her honeymoon and has now passed away.

‌



The German content creator, who had more than 51,000 Instagram followers, had married her husband Tilman only days earlier before the couple headed to the mountains for their honeymoon.

‌



The crash happened on the Passo Sella mountain pass on June 23. Laura was descending a series of bends when she collided head-on with a motorcycle being ridden uphill by former Italian downhill skier Peter Runggaldier, according to local reports. The 57-year-old previously won two Alpine Ski World Cup races.

View 3 Images Laura was a fitness influencer (Image: Jam Press/@alltimelaura)

Ryanair issues airport delay warning to UK families over 15 destinations – list READ MORE :

The impact was so severe that Laura's bicycle was reportedly snapped in two, with both riders thrown several metres onto the road.

‌



Emergency crews, including two rescue helicopters, rushed to the scene before Laura was airlifted to hospital in Bolzano in a critical condition.

She was later transferred to a specialist clinic in Bavaria, Germany, to be closer to her family. Despite doctors' efforts, Laura died from her injuries on Sunday after spending almost three weeks in intensive care.

View 3 Images Laura died following a road collision (Image: Jam Press/@alltimelaura)

‌



Runggaldier, who reportedly suffered multiple fractures and abdominal injuries, survived the crash. Investigators are continuing to examine the circumstances surrounding the collision.

"Regarding the serious road accident I was involved in, I ask you to respect my moment of grief and my need for privacy," he wrote on Instagram. "My thoughts are with all those involved and their families. I trust in your compassion,"

Laura was well known online for sharing videos of hiking, cycling and outdoor adventures in the Alps.

‌



In a heartbreaking final Instagram post shared just weeks before the crash, she uploaded footage from her wedding ceremony in the Dolomites, showing the couple exchanging vows surrounded by mountains and loved ones. The clip was captioned: "Soulmate for life."

A statement from Italian police on Facebook said: "Road accident. This morning the force attended a road accident at Passo Sella, kilometer 32+400.

Article continues below

"A motorcycle and a bicycle were involved. Traffic was stuck for about an hour. Intervened in support of the Canazei VVF, the White Cross of Canazei, Trentino emergency and the helicopter services."

News.title: Bodybuilder suddenly collapses and dies just days before major competition
News.content:
Bodybuilder suddenly collapses and dies just days before major competition

Bodybuilding influencer Mailson Araújo, 35, was preparing for a competition and had just finished a workout when he suddenly died at his home in Brazil

View 3 Images Mailson Araújo has died in Brazil (Image: JamPress)

A bodybuilding influencer collapsed and died suddenly shortly after returning home from a workout.

‌



Mailson Araújo, who was preparing for a major professional competition, died at home in Alagoinhas, Brazil on Monday evening.

‌



The 35-year-old immediately felt unwell and called his parents for help after getting back from the training session. His mother, a nurse, attempted CPR but he could not be revived despite efforts by firefighters and emergency services at the scene.

‌



Mailson, a professional Men's Physique athlete with more than 32,000 Instagram fans, was pronounced dead at the home. Hours earlier, he had posted videos and photos of his gym workout and physiotherapy session on social media.

View 3 Images The 35-year-old immediately felt unwell after a workout (Image: JamPress)

Mum nearly fainted over what Google revealed about her new boyfriend READ MORE :

The exact cause of death has not yet been confirmed by the authorities. Tributes have poured in from the bodybuilding community.

‌



One page wrote: "Brazil Bodybuilding News offers its most sincere condolences to his friends, family and the entire bodybuilding community.

“May God comfort everyone's hearts in this very difficult moment."

Mailson turned professional in 2023 after winning the amateur title at the Arnold Classic South America in São Paulo.

‌



He earned several strong placings, including third at Musclecontest Brazil 2023, fifth in his pro debut at Bahia Pro 2023, and additional top-four finishes.

View 3 Images The exact cause of death has not yet been confirmed (Image: JamPress)

He was set to compete at the prestigious Musclecontest Brazil 2026 this weekend in Curitiba, marking a return to the stage after a lighter competitive schedule.

Article continues below

Mailson worked as an online sports consultant alongside his athletic career, regularly sharing training, nutrition and recovery content with his fans.

Friends and followers left messages of sorrow on his final Instagram posts.

His body was laid to rest at the Jardim Paraíso da Saudade Cemetery in Alagoinhas.

News.title: Tesco trials huge change to UK supermarkets as ‘6ft AI robot’ spotted in store
News.content:
Tesco trials huge change to UK supermarkets as ‘6ft AI robot’ spotted in store

A new life-sized robot is being trialed in Tesco to detect missing stock and pricing mistakes - and to save staff from having to carry out manual checks

View 2 Images The robots use AI to scan supermarket aisles (Image: Jam Press/Simbe)

Tesco is trialing a new 6.5ft aisle-roaming robot to help detect missing stock and pricing errors.

‌



The life-sized machine will use AI and computer vision to independently roam supermarket aisles and continuously monitor shelves - saving staff from having to carry out manual checks.

‌



Tesco said the Tally robot by Simbe Robotics will also help spot gaps on shelves so that staff can better boost visibility. According to Simbe, Tally can spot 10 times more out-of-stock products than those found in manual checks.

‌



The machine can also pick up on pricing errors and items displayed in the wrong location, then send over reports to store colleagues so that the issues can be quickly resolved.

Posting an image of the bot at a Tesco store, one Reddit user said: "Walked into my local Tesco to see a 'Inventory Checking' robot going about the store.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



"Even more hilarious than it being called Tally is that nobody went within 5ft of it and kept giving it sideye."

Industry expert Toby Pickard, Retail Futures Senior Partner at IGD, revealed the trial after spotting the robot operating inside a Tesco store.

He said the move marks Tesco's first deployment of autonomous shelf-scanning technology and only the second time a major UK supermarket has trialled the system.

‌



"This marks a first for Tesco in the UK and only the second time we've seen a major UK retailer trialling autonomous shelf-scanning technology," he wrote in a post on LinkedIn.

"Rather than relying on manual audits, the robot captures shelf conditions multiple times a day and provides store teams with prioritised action lists via mobile apps and digital or printed reports.

"The goal is simple: resolve issues faster, improve inventory accuracy, and free up colleagues to spend more time serving customers."

‌



View 2 Images The Tally robot is being used at retailers in multiple other countries (Image: Jam Press/Simbe)

Tally, which was first introduced a decade ago, has already been used across retailers in several other countries.

Morrisons was the first UK supermarket to trial the machine last year, introducing it at stores in Wetherby, Redcar and Stockton.

‌



Those robots measured roughly 5ft4 inches in height and travelled across shop floors without assistance - using sensors to move around obstacles.

The new bots being used for the Tesco trial are reportedly 6.5ft tall.

During the Morrisons trial, the robot was used to check product placement and availability, and help ensure the correct pricing information was being displayed.

Article continues below

The supermarket introduced the technology to reduce the amount of time colleagues spent carrying out routine shelf inspections, allowing them to focus on assisting customers instead.

News.title: Starmer says it's the 'end of my political journey' at his final Prime Minister's Questions
News.content:
Chancellor Rachel Reeves - who was at Sir Keir's side on the front bench as usual - appeared close to tears.

Labour MP Carolyn Harris was also overcome by emotion as she told MPs that "every day we see his decency and his courage shine through".

Sir Keir is due to hand over power to Andy Burnham on Monday, after the former Greater Manchester mayor is confirmed as Labour leader at a special Labour conference on Friday.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch refrained from attacking the outgoing PM's record, instead praising him for his work on Ukraine and his friendship with the country's president Volodymyr Zelensky.

But she did aim some jibes at Labour MPs and their next leader, who was absent from the session as he has been at all the PMQs sessions since he returned to Parliament last month.

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey said Sir Keir had worked with people across the House of Commons and described him as a "true patriot".

Watching on were several guests of the prime minister including campaigners he had met during his time in Downing Street.

He addressed some of them directly as he spoke, saying: "To all those in the gallery whose lives have been changed or improved by this Labour government, and all across the country who struggle to be seen or heard, you're the reason I came into politics."

Despite being forced out by his own MPs just two years after winning a landslide election victory, Sir Keir was met with cheers from the Labour benches as he arrived in the House of Commons.

As is often the case for a prime minister's final question session, the tone was gentler and more light-hearted than usual, with plenty of jokes about England's World Cup hopes as well as the by-election in Clacton.

However, it began on a sombre note with Sir Keir paying tribute to former MP Ann Widdecombe.

He said it was "chilling" that during his time in Parliament three serving or former MPs had been killed.

Badenoch paid tribute to the former Conservative minister as a woman of "high principle" with a "wicked sense of humour".

News.title: Iain Watson: Burnham faces crucial choice for chancellor as battle for No 11 continues
News.content:
The battle for Number 10 is over.

An overwhelming number of Labour MPs have nominated Andy Burnham. Under Labour's rules he needs trade union support too.

He crossed that threshold today. He is moving into Number 10 on Monday.

But the beneath-the-radar battle for Number 11 Downing St is continuing. Whoever Burnham appoints as chancellor - and next-door neighbour in Downing Street - will send a signal of his intent both to politicians and to the bond markets.

The official line from team Burnham is that no decision has been taken.

Announcements on cabinet posts are not expected to be made until Monday, when Burnham moves to Number 10.

Discussions have been taking place amongst a tight group of people - the next Number 10 chief of staff James Purnell, Louise Haigh and the former MP who stood aside for Burnham, Josh Simons.

When Burnham won the subsequent Makerfield by-election the widespread assumption was that the Energy Secretary Ed Miliband would move to the Treasury.

But there has been both noisy and more subtle attempts to influence Burnham's choice of chancellor - ranging from unions with workers in the oil and gas industry and who distrust Miliband's instincts, to Sir Keir Starmer's unpaid 'cost of living' tsar Lord Walker, the boss of Iceland.

He runs supermarkets but argues that it's the bond markets that would "freak out" if an "ideological" chancellor was installed in the Treasury.

In recent days, a number of MPs close to Burnham - who have no animus to the energy secretary - believe the likelihood of appointing Miliband has lessened significantly.

The caveat is that they are not making the decisions, but are discerning the mood.

Those close to Miliband believe that it's not only highly possible that he will still be appointed but highly desirable too.

They point to his credentials. He has an economics background, was an adviser in the Treasury under Gordon Brown and chaired the Council of Economic Advisers.

He has ministerial experience in the last Labour government and this one. He knows his way around. A colleague put it like this: "He can make the Treasury do what it doesn't want to do."

Miliband has offered advice to Burnham regularly and recently and would be in lock-step with Burnham in the task of spreading growth, in Burnham's words, "to every postcode".

As for the bond markets, one supporter has stressed his adherence to the fiscal rules on debt and borrowing, and another put it more colourfully: "He isn't Che Guevara."

Many in the parliamentary party would expect him to move to Number 11. If he isn't, some on the party's soft left will think that Burnham has refused the first fence in the race to change Britain.

News.title: Man arrested over social media post threatening to shoot Farage
News.content:
A man has been arrested over an alleged threat to shoot Reform UK leader Nigel Farage made in a social media post.

The arrest relates to a post made on X which was reported to police on 8 May, a day after the local and mayoral elections.

The Met Police said a man in his 20s was arrested in south London on Tuesday this week on suspicion of sending threatening communications to a Member of Parliament.

He has been bailed pending further inquiries.

The arrest came six days after Reform spokesperson Ann Widdecombe was killed at her Devon home. Counter terror police are investigating the death.

The Parliamentary Liaison and Investigation Team informed Farage of the arrest on Wednesday.

Farage said: "This is the first time the police have ever proactively acted on a social media post, and I hope they are looking at the other three or four hundred similar posts from this year alone."

The arrest was first reported in the Daily Telegraph newspaper,, external which said the social media post warned Farage: "I am going to shoot you in the head if you win".

Police told Farage it could take several weeks to examine digital devices they had seized.

Earlier on Wednesday Reform UK's home affairs spokesperson said if the party was in government it would provide "round-the-clock protection" for all MPs.

Announcing the proposed policy at a press conference, Zia Yusuf also said Farage "lives his life under the ever-present threat of mortal danger" and those who "question his need for security should stop".

News.title: The Odyssey is a 'colossal piece of cinema', critics say in rave reviews
News.content:
The Odyssey, the latest film from Oscar-winning director Sir Christopher Nolan, has received rapturous reviews from critics.

The film, adapted from Homer's epic ancient Greek poem, is Nolan's first since 2023's Oppenheimer, which won the Academy Award for best picture.

The Telegraph described The Odyssey as the "film of the year", while Metro declared that the movie would "change cinema forever".

The Times, meanwhile, described it as "a masterpiece in every way", and the Standard praised the film as a "colossal piece of cinema".

The Odyssey, which will be released in the UK on Friday, stars Matt Damon, Zendaya, Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, Anne Hathaway, Charlize Theron and Lupita Nyong'o.

It follows Odysseus (Damon), the Greek king of Ithaca, on his long and perilous journey home from the Trojan War to rescue his wife and son (Hathaway and Holland).

His fantastical journey sees him encounter mythical beings along the way. Meanwhile, the cruel antagonist Antinous has his eyes fixed on the queen while her husband is still away.

News.title: Dramatic video shows wildfire surround freight train in Canada
News.content:
Video captured on 13 July shows a wildfire surrounding a freight train in Ontario, Canada. CN Rail told the BBC that it temporarily suspended operations in the area and relocated employees. The workers seen in the video were able to escape and are safe. Currently, there are multiple wildfires burning across the northwestern part of the province, with numerous fires remaining out of control due to extreme heat, dry conditions, and strong winds.

Read more on this story

News.title: SpaceX share price drops below stock market debut
News.content:
SpaceX's share price has dropped below its stock market debut just over a month ago, falling sharply from a post-float peak.

The price for a single share in Elon Musk's rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence (AI) company fell to $132.62 (Â£98.24) on Wednesday, below its initial listing of $135 in June.

SpaceX's initial public offering (IPO) made Musk the world's first trillionaire. Compared to its on-the-day high so far, the stock price is now down 41%.

If the price holds, or falls further, it will mean that those who purchased stock around the time of its flotation will stand to lose money on their investment.

Even amid a tumultuous few weeks for tech stocks, SpaceX has taken a particular hit.

Compared to a 0.2% fall on the wider Nasdaq index, where SpaceX's shares are listed, the company's stock price fell more than 2% on Wednesday.

SpaceX stock has been volatile since it began trading on the public stock market a little over one month ago.

After an initial investor frenzy that saw the company valued at more than Amazon and Microsoft, the price of its shares has drifted downward.

Initially, SpaceX was treated by investors as the first chance they had to invest in an AI company, according to what financial market analysts and experts recently told the BBC,

Earlier this year, SpaceX acquired Musk's AI start-up xAI, recently renamed SpaceXAI, marking it's first foray into an AI-focused business.

XAI is best known for the controversial chatbot Grok, but through that acquisition, SpaceX now leases data centre capacity to other tech companies.

The company's main business is the manufacture and launch of rockets and telecommunications satellites called Starlink.

When Starlink said it was cutting prices in the Memphis, Tennessee area amid local concerns over a massive data centre project, SpaceX shares fell by 8%.

Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers, told Reuters: "There hasn't been anything that lately to remind people of some of the catalysts for why they bought SpaceX."

SpaceX is expected to release in August its first public earnings report.

Sosnick added: "The fact that a stock has fallen a couple of dollars below its IPO price in itself is not a tragedy, but SpaceX is heavily watched and has an important role in investor psyche."

SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

News.title: Covid fraudsters spent thousands on cars and watches
News.content:
Fraudsters who carried out a personal protective equipment (PPE) scam during the Covid-19 pandemic spent hundreds of thousands of pounds on luxury cars, watches and home renovations.

Jogesh Bhandari, 59, and Craig Morris, 43, were convicted on Wednesday at Leicester Crown Court following a trial of two counts of conspiracy to commit fraud by false representation as well as concealing and transferring criminal property.

Meenakashi Bhandari, 48, was found guilty of concealing and transferring criminal property. The National Crime Agency (NCA) said the group claimed they could supply millions of boxes of nitrile gloves.

They are due to be sentenced on 21 August.

The NCA said bank records showed that Jogesh Bhandari and his wife, Meenakashi Bhandari, both of Mitchell Drive in Loughborough, Leicestershire, used the money to buy Rolexes, jewellery, holiday packages and cars.

Jogesh spent Â£126,000 on a new Porsche while other cash was used for a kitchen refurbishment, the NCA said.

According to the NCA, Jogesh owned and controlled a company set up in 2020 to buy and sell nitrile gloves, while Morris helped in a number of fraudulent deals in 2020 and 2021.

The agency said Jogesh supplied a number of forged documents to potential suppliers, including bank statements showing up to $125m and letters of attestation to try and persuade businesses to trade with him.

News.title: UK's extreme weather is the new normal, Met Office says
News.content:
Weather that was once considered extreme is becoming the "new normal", according to the latest Met Office report on the UK's climate.

It shows the hottest day of the year in the south of England is now typically 4.5C warmer than it was in 1961-1990.

The scientists say that the country's climate is "on the move" as northern areas of Britain now see warmer temperatures that used to only affect southern England.

Homes, schools, hospitals, and transport networks are struggling to cope with back-to-back heatwaves this summer, exposing how unprepared the UK is for climate change.

News.title: Burnham does not rule out wealth tax
News.content:
Andy Burnham has not ruled out a wealth tax, suggesting his incoming government may have "to ask for a little more" tax at some point.

Burnham, who is due to become prime minister on Monday, was asked whether he was considering a wealth tax in an interview, external with former footballer and Match of the Day presenter Gary Lineker.

The Labour MP said he would take time to review the state of the public finances and wanted to focus on "bringing people together" rather than creating "new divisions".

"I'm not going rule things out right now," Burnham said. "I do believe we need a greater sense of fairness."

The former Greater Manchester mayor said "decisions to be taken in time" were "going to be difficult".

"I'm not going to shy away from that," Burnham said. "You know, we are going to have to work quite hard to make sure, you know, we can pay our way.

"And at some point that might be having to ask for a little more. But, you know, those decisions are not for now. They're for another day."

Burnham has not set out in detail what tax policies he would pursue since he declared his intention to replace Sir Keir Starmer as Labour leader and prime minister, following his by-election win in Makerfield last month.

He has given a few clues in interviews, including one with LBC, in which he said he felt there was "some room" for movement on tax.

Burnham suggested business rates on warehouses could be increased to fund tax cuts for pubs and some high-street businesses.

But the Makerfield MP said he would stick to the pledges Labour made not to raise VAT, income tax or national insurance in its general election manifesto in 2024.

With options for raising revenue limited outside of these manifesto commitments, some Labour MPs on the left of the party, economists and campaigners have suggested a tax on wealth.

One proposal - backed by Oxfam and Tax Justice UK among others - is a 2% levy on assets over Â£10m.

The Green Party of England and Wales backs a similar policy, a wealth tax of 1% annually on assets above Â£10m and of 2% on assets above Â£1bn.

Reform UK's Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said Burnham had admitted "people will have to pay more in tax" in his interview with Lineker.

"He should rule out the ten taxes - Â£3,450 for every family - he's previously supported but has no mandate for," Jenrick wrote in a post on X.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said Burnham was not even prime minister yet "but he's already talking about raising your taxes again".

"We are heading for another summer of chaos with Labour obsessing about who they can tax to pay for more benefits," Badenoch said.

News.title: Three men who raped woman on Brighton beach jailed
News.content:
Three men who raped a woman on Brighton beach in an "entirely predatory, callous and contemptuous" attack have been jailed.

Asylum seekers Abdulla Ahmadi, Ibrahim Alshafe and Karin Al-Danasurt attacked the woman in the early hours of 4 October.

The victim, who jurors heard was "led into the darkness to be used as a sexual plaything", said she still heard their laughter when she closed her eyes, adding: "My skin crawls - no matter how hard I scrub it I still feel dirty."

Ahmadi, 26, from Iran, and Alshafe, 26, from Egypt, were each jailed for 21 years. Al-Danasurt, 21, also from Egypt, was convicted of rape as a secondary party for filming the attack and was jailed for 18 years and six months.

Sentencing the three men at Hove Crown Court, Her Honour Judge Christine Henson KC said each of them "participated in an entirely predatory and callous attack".

She added: "The impact on your victim was and continues to be devastating. It has had a life changing profound and irrevocable impact on her."

Each of the men, who were living in a Home Office hotel in Horsham at the time of the offence, will also spend a further six years on extended licence, and will serve two thirds of their sentence before they can be considered for parole.

Warning: Some readers may find the following details distressing.

The court previously heard from prosecutor Hanna Llewellyn-Waters KC, who said the three men were "on the lookout for women that night for sexual purposes" as they visited bars and nightclubs on Brighton seafront.

After leaving a club, the men crossed paths with the woman, who cannot be identified for legal reasons, at a fast-food restaurant and they all went to the beach.

Jurors heard the woman was "staggering in the street" and was "incapacitated".

Alshafe and Ahmadi took her behind a beach hut, where they raped her while Al-Danasurt filmed the ordeal.

The trial heard the woman recalled being spat on, kicked and her throat being grabbed during the attack.

News.title: Boy, 14, charged over alleged plan to target mosques
News.content:
A 14-year-old boy has been charged with a terrorism offence after police discovered an alleged plan to target two London mosques that was linked to "extreme right-wing terrorism".

The child was initially arrested at an address in south London on suspicion of criminal damage to a vehicle, but officers found "a number of documents of concern", the Metropolitan Police said.

He is accused of planning to target the two places of worship in Sutton and has been remanded in custody.

He is due at Westminster Magistratesâ Court on Thursday charged with preparation of terrorist acts on or before 9 July, and racially aggravated damage to property, the force said.

Det Ch Supt Nick Blackburn, in charge of local policing for the south London area, said: "These charges come just days after 12 people were arrested for a suspected threat to an Islamic festival in Suffolk and a man was arrested for an alleged assault outside a mosque in Leyton."

He added: "We should not underestimate the cumulative impact of incidents of this nature on the Muslim community."

Cdr Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) London, said it was a "very serious terrorism charge against a young boy" and "particularly concerning" to the Muslim community.

She said they were seeing an increasing number of children and young people in their casework.

The Met said it had been working closely with counter terrorism teams on the probe and had increased patrols in affected areas.

There is not believed to be "any enduring or wider threat" and police are not seeking anyone else in connection with the incidents, a statement said.

News.title: Peers face new attendance rules under proposed House of Lords changes
News.content:
Peers who fail to turn up regularly enough to the House of Lords could be kicked out of Parliament, under new committee proposals.

In its 2024 manifesto, the Labour government promised to introduce a retirement age and participation requirement for members of the upper chamber and the Lords committee was set up to recommend ways of implementing the change.

In its report, published on Wednesday, external, the committee recommended phasing in a retirement age of 80 and requiring members to attend at least 20% of sitting days.

Committee chair Baroness Taylor of Bolton said the move was a "practical solution" that would ensure the "continued effective functioning of the House".

A government spokesperson said: "Introducing a retirement age and participation requirement to the House of Lords is a manifesto commitment, and we will therefore carefully consider the committee's recommendations ahead of the government's response later this year."

There have been concern for many years about the size of the House of Lords, which currently stands at 774, making it one of the largest upper parliamentary houses in the world.

Earlier this year, the numbers were slightly reduced after 92 hereditary peers - those who inherited their place in the House of Lords from their parents - were removed, although 15 were subsequently given life peerages.

The House of Lords Retirement and Participation Committee recommended that a new retirement age of 80 should apply to all existing members "without exception".

However, it said that in order to avoid a "cliff edge" with several peers leaving at the same time, the retirement threshold should be phased in gradually.

Under the proposals, the latest age at which a peer should retire would be set at 85 from 8 July 2029 and then reduced by one year annually eventually reaching 80 by July 2034.

New members would be asked to agree in writing that they would retire by their 80th birthday.

Currently peers are required to attend the House of Lords at least once in a session.

The committee said this was "too low and reform is necessary". It recommended increasing the threshold to 20% of sitting days, averaged out over two sessions.

The number of days in a parliamentary session vary but over the last 10 years have been an average of around 170 days.

The committee said it recognised that "short-term absences may arise without notice in cases of emergency or on compassionate grounds".

"Such circumstances should be taken into account to ensure that members are not inappropriately penalised for failing to meet the attendance threshold," it said.

A House of Lords briefing has estimated, external that by July 2029, 301 life peers would be aged over 80.

The average age of the House of Lords is currently 70-years-old.

News.title: Tommy Robinson says he 'got it wrong' over man he falsely accused of filming children
News.content:
Far-right activist Tommy Robinson has admitted he "got it wrong" when he falsely accused a man on social media of filming children in a Glasgow park.

Footage of UK-born Quoroum Beg with a mobile phone in his hand began circulating last Sunday, with Robinson labelling him an "invader".

Beg was in fact filming an anti-immigration demonstration which had earlier forced him and his children, along with other families, to leave the park in the city's Gorbals area.

Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, has now issued a correction on X, saying: "In this instance I got it wrong, as did many others, so for that I apologise and have deleted that post."

However Beg told BBC Scotland News that Robinson's correction appears to fall far short of an apology.

"Is he apologising because he can't get his facts right or is he apologising for the hurt he's caused me?" he said.

Beg - who has three children and works full-time in Glasgow - now fears for his safety. He has been given an emergency police number to call in case he feels threatened.

News.title: Salary information to be shown on job ads under new laws
News.content:
Employers will have to publish salary information in job adverts under government plans to rewrite anti-discrimination laws.

Details of other job conditions could also have to be disclosed to candidates, under the draft proposals.

Ministers argue greater transparency will help people navigate the jobs market and could prevent future pay discrimination claims.

However, details of exactly what salary information will have to be shared are yet to be hammered out.

Officials plan to consult on whether exact salaries will have to be displayed, or potentially a pay range or "benchmark rate" for open roles.

They also plan to ask industry groups whether information beyond basic salary, such as bonuses, should be made available.

Employers that do not publish a job advert for a role would have to give candidates the information in writing prior to a job interview.

In a policy document, the Cabinet Office said salary information would help jobseekers make informed application decisions, and improve the hiring process for companies by weeding out candidates with "misaligned pay expectations".

Citing various academic studies, it also said transparency would help prevent "unequal outcomes" when salaries are offered to successful applicants.

"When pay is opaque, salary decisions can be influenced by stereotypes â such as stereotypes of women, ethnic minorities, or disabled people," it added.

News.title: Dartmoor ponies given new protection after cull fears
News.content:
Dartmoor ponies will be protected at their current levels following fears of a potential cull, ministers have said.

Campaigners had raised concerns that new Natural England contracts requiring reduced grazing on the Devon moor's commons could lead to the removal of up to 90% of the ponies.

But the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said the animals will be removed from stocking rate calculations - meaning farmers would not face a choice between keeping ponies and maintaining sheep or cattle.

Defra said the long-term future of the ponies had been secured through a package of "new protections and financial support".

Pony numbers will be monitored across the moor to make sure they remain stable, the government added.

Dartmoor hill ponies have been part of the landscape for 4,500 years, but their numbers have dropped from 6,000 25 years ago to fewer than 1,000 today, and the breed has now been declared endangered.

News.title: Mocking regional accents is last form of acceptable discrimination, says MP
News.content:
Northumbrian MP Ian Lavery has claimed mocking people with strong regional accents is the last form of acceptable discrimination.

The Labour MP for Blyth and Ashington joined fellow MPs railing against those who look down on people because of how they speak, during a debate in Parliament.

Jo Platt, the Labour MP for Leigh and Atherton, led the Westminster Hall debate on regional accents and social mobility, explaining the pressure on people to change the way they speak in order to progress in life.

The debate came as Andy Burnham, who was born in Merseyside and raised in Culcheth near Warrington, is about to become the prime minister.

Burnham has proposed a programme of devolution, including setting up a No 10 North, and MPs said the UK should also regain its pride in the cultural depth of regional accents.

Lavery said his accent was from the coal mines and showed who he was, where he was from and who he represented, but highlighted how there was still a stigma attached to strong accents by employers, forming a barrier for working class children.

"Many people are forced between maintaining an accent they're proud of or indeed ditching their accent to try to just even move on in life," he said.

"It's just not right - it's the last form of acceptable discrimination in this country and it's absolutely ridiculous."

He added: "It's the one that we suffer from the most - the social markers, the local dialect, who you are, and where you should be in life, because of how you speak."

Such accent bias can hold people back, agreed Platt, who said: "Long before we explain our politics, our profession, or our background, the moment we open our mouths our accents instantly signal a core part of who we are."

Platt said these barriers are not spoken about enough, saying that as a working class woman from Salford, she had also felt pressure to speak with a more neutral accent.

"I will admit there was a time when I wondered if softening my accent might make me sound more credible, more professional, more 'Westminster'," she said, adding: "I worried that the way I spoke would limit my prospects so I toned my accent down."
